_readme: Settings for provisioning/dataverse/verify-access-test-identity.ps1 -Env dev ONLY.
NEW 2026-08-23 — improvement review 18, changes 1 and 2 (IMP-0228, IMP-0153, IMP-0221).
WHY THIS FILE IS NOT dev-settings.json. Get-ProvisioningSettings -Env dev MUST keep
throwing 'file not found': src/tests/provisioning/ProvisioningCommon.Tests.ps1 asserts
that throw by name, and several scripts rely on it as the signal that DEV has nothing of
that kind scripted against it. Same dedicated-file pattern as dev-schema-settings.json,
dev-scoring-settings.json and dev-auditing-settings.json. The verifier reads THIS file
directly on -Env dev, bypassing Get-ProvisioningSettings entirely, so that invariant is
undisturbed. scripts/verify-pipeline-config.py check 13 recognises the pattern by the
single-quoted filename literal in the script.
WHY THE COMPARISON IDENTITY IS PINNED BY NAME. On 2026-08-23 the V4 step's own prose said
'confirm membership live and add one identity if there is none' and named no identity. A
human satisfied it by adding the TRUSTEE TEST ACCOUNT as a direct member of
REV_TrusteeRestricted — the one account that must never be a member, because membership
grants read on the twelve columns the access test exists to prove are hidden. The letter of
the instruction was met and its purpose was destroyed. So the two identities are declared
here, separately, and the verifier fails if they are the same systemuserid.
Identifiers only — never a secret, token or connection string (C-TECH-001). The provisioning
app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the environment variables named under 'auth'.
Values are UPNs, not GUIDs, deliberately: a systemuserid differs per environment, and a
hand-copied GUID is how IMP-0157 shipped a fabricated one. The verifier resolves each UPN
to exactly one enabled systemuser at run time and fails if it resolves to zero or many.
The observed DEV ids are recorded as comments for cross-checking only and are never read.

dataverse._comment_environmentUrl: Environment REV-GrantApplications-DEV. Same values as dev-schema-settings.json and dev-auditing-settings.json.

accessTest._comment: The WBS 6.5 trustee access test (config/revitalise-grant-automation-pipeline.yml, verification level V4). C-TECH-068.
accessTest._comment_testIdentityUpn: The NEGATIVE control: the person who signs in and must see the identifying columns EMPTY. Observed DEV systemuserid 678354c5-cc9e-f111-b8de-7ced8d43e1b4 (logs/pipeline.log 2026-08-23 11:20). Resolved live by UPN, never from that id.
accessTest._comment_permittedRoles: The COMPLETE set of security roles the test identity may hold. Any additional role invalidates the test, because a role carrying System Administrator bypasses column security entirely and the trustee would see everything. Observed DEV roleid for REV Trustee: 3ab6cc7b-959d-f111-b8de-70a8a5079a1b. Roles are matched BY NAME because role GUIDs differ per environment (C-TECH-040, ADR-008).
accessTest._comment_comparisonIdentityUpn: The POSITIVE control: the identity that IS released the columns, so that 'the trustee saw nulls' can be distinguished from 'everyone sees nulls' (IMP-0110). MUST be a different person from testIdentityUpn — that is the check that today's defect defeated. This account is a test fixture for the comparison read, not a grant of standing access to a person.
accessTest._comment_securedProfileHint: NOT read by the verifier and NOT a list to maintain: the verifier ENUMERATES fieldsecurityprofiles live, so a profile created after this file was written is still checked. Recorded only so a human reading this file knows which profile the test is about: REV_TrusteeRestricted, fieldsecurityprofileid 5fd58153-e997-f111-b8dc-7ced8d43e1b4 (src/solutions/RevitaliseGrantAutomation/Other/FieldSecurityProfiles.xml).
